source: Ah. My God. You lost it, didn't you?
In a manner of speaking. But it's somewhere in the castle. I believe.
He's going to kill me.
Not that I'm frightened of Laertes, or anything. I'm not. Of course.
It could only be in a couple of places, truly. My memory is ever-so-slightly hazy.
However, I seem to recall there was one night we took the lute up on the walls.
We were all three together, were we not? And I had it then. I know I did.
The walls! Of course! The blasted walls. It's got to be up there!
Let us meet when we have a moment from our respective duties.
Goodness. I don't often take the patrol up here. I forget how cold and damp it is.
That damn lute has to be here somewhere.
I would have expected it to be here.
I don't see it.
Neither do I. And besides, even if it were here, it'd be soaked through with seaward mist.
Laertes is going to throttle us both.
You're stronger than he is. My money's on you.
That is decidedly not the point here.
What? Worried you haven't kept your sparring skills up-to-date?
En garde.
Ow! What was that for?
Come, now. It was merely the flat of the blade. Aren't you going to dodge?
To show you the flat of my blade would be unseemly for a man of my role.
Ow! Stop! All right, point-- made-- Bernardo. Stop!
As you wish, my lord.
No, wait. Don't grow serious, now. I was only joking. We can continue sparring.
I think that's quite enough for now, my lord. Were I to injure you, it would draw significant ire.
I remember when we used to spar all morning as boys, and I'd come home with bruises.
I guess some things have changed.
You are much more a prince and much less a boy, for one.
Suppose so.
Well, in any case, the lute isn't here.
If Laertes were here, I'm certain he'd remember.
Might it not be in the woods by the pond? I seem to recall us going out there the last time you were home from Wittenberg.
Indeed. When it's next convenient, let's meet and search the woods.
I don't believe I've been out here in quite some time.
This is the only place I can stop and think a while. It can be so stifling in there.
'There'? The castle, you mean?
Yes. All those eyes around. Here, the only things watching are birds.
Now—where would that lute be?
In the brush, I imagine. Over here.
Say, Bernardo.
It feels as though it's been ages since you and I had a real conversation. It has, hasn't it?
Years, I wager.
Are you well? Are you happy? Getting on? With the guard, and all?
My lord, I find your sudden concern for others extremely unusual, and therefore upsetting. But yes, I'm all right.
These days, it seems as though there's a cloud over you. There's something strange about you.
Most would say the same about you, my lord.
That's the problem with growing old. We were carefree once. Now things are different.
And so they are.
Say, Bernardo. What we saw that night—my father's ghost—that was real, wasn't it? I didn't dream it? I'm not mad, am I?
Not at all, my lord. Did you ever doubt?
I... I think I did, a little. I don't know what to do. I want to forget what I saw. But I can't, I can't, all I do is see his face, burned into the back of my mind—
My lord, perhaps it is the devil speaking to you. Or perhaps it is a sign. I know not which.
A sign of what?
Bernardo, what is this distance I feel?
I know... I haven't been the most ardent friend lately. But I knew everything about you once, and you me.
Can we not be that way once more? I am in short supply of men I can trust these days.
My lord, the things which weigh on my mind would only make your humor worse, and would improve little for me.
Is it because you're Katherine more and more these days?
I hadn't thought of it. In some ways, perhaps, I am becoming more myself.
And I am mourning the person I left behind.
For what it's worth, I don't mourn that person. And I would like to know you as you are.
I am honored, my Prince. But right now...
Please. Focus on yourself, on your own health. For Denmark's sake. We need you.
Wait a moment...
H-here. The lute! Look.
You found it?
And it's entirely dry. A miracle, if I've seen one.
I wish I knew how to make this right, Bernardo. But Laertes is gone.
Indeed. If only Laertes were here, we could give it to him.
I'm certain he's playing some other, better lute in Paris.
Yes. When he returns, you ought to give this back to him swiftly. Perhaps even make proper amends.
Until then, I bid you good-bye. I've my rounds to make.
See you about, friend.
(I know if Laertes were here, things would've gone differently.)
(There's more to this situation.)
I'd like to make things right with Laertes.
Indeed. Since he has remained in Elsinore, I'll return it to him anon.
No. Allow me. I've been avoiding Laertes far too long. I'll put an end to this constant back-and-forth between us.
Is that wise, my lord?
Let me be the judge of that.
Thought I'd find you here.
Come to insult me, then?
No. To make a return, in fact.
I have something of yours.
My lute. I knew you'd stolen it.
I didn't. But you won't believe me, regardless.
You're right. Put it over there, and leave.
You know, Laertes...
You're the consummate gentleman. Everyone in Elsinore admires you so.
Even my uncle, a man who bends to no one, gives you his ear freely.
All I ever wanted was a sliver of that same admiration.
But you've hated me all these years, haven't you?
I can feel your stare upon my back wherever I go.
You tore my sister's heart open. Who wouldn't hate you?
You detested me long before that. Let us not pretend this is some new grievance.
You gallivant around in your own little world, paying no mind to the needs of the country you will someday run.
Is that not reason enough to hate you?
If I were meant to run this country, I would already be doing so. I'm but a stallion for show. Nobody wants me to wear the crown.
I'll be honest, Laertes. I came here hoping to forge a peace.
It is hard enough to think of wearing my father's crown with so few of his friends willing to stand at my side.
You murdered my father, Hamlet.
You murdered him, and then you hid his body, and you continued to bury your head in the sand.
How can you be so naïve as to think you and I could ever be friends? In this world, or the next?
I learned a new language of hatred in order to know my own feelings for you.
I didn't know what it was to hate anyone like this. Until now.
You destroyed my sister's happiness, neglected your country, and abandoned your father's legacy.
All of these things I despise. All things which sap my respect.
Get out.
Get out, now. Leave the lute and go.
I can never fix the horrible things I've done to you over the years, Laertes.
I swear to you it was a mistake. I didn't mean to hurt your father.
I'm not like you. My mind doesn't work like yours. Something's broken in my head, I think.
And I wish with all my soul it could be otherwise.
Do you think I enjoy disappointing everyone? No one does. But please believe me—
I never meant to cause you harm.
So if you would continue to despise me in light of that, then I urge you: Kill me.
Kill me, and have your peace.
Hamlet. What trick is this?
It is no trick. I have wanted to die for months. Please. I'm exhausted.
Everyone hates me, but none more than I hate myself. And I'm ready. May it bring you comfort and vengeance.
I... thought I wanted your death.
I don't want your death, Hamlet.
But I do seek your destruction, of a sort.
...The destruction of your family line, and its undue influence upon my country.
The men of your line have brought this country to its knees, embattled it in needless wars, and drained its coffers.
And I have no reason to believe you will be any stronger or better than they were.
If anything, I see many of their vices reflected back in you.
So—you and I—we cannot be allies.
And now that I vote on behalf of our lands in my father's place, I will never alight upon you as my King.
I shall work to turn the nobility against you.
...Even if you prove to me that you can do otherwise. I know who you are. And who you have been, and will always be.
You will never be a King.
That's all I want.
Your uncle asked me to kill you, Hamlet.
What? Truly?
He posted a formal challenge of a duel between us. But the duel won't be a fair one.
He has poisoned a blade for me to use against you—and a goblet of wine as a fallback.
And I agreed to help him kill you.
But I cannot.
This is wrong. My father would never have asked for this.
I think you and I ought to forge a truce.
Y-you mean it?
I mean it.
Your uncle is a vile man. This, I know. His people are summarily displeased with his rule.
I came back to Elsinore to depose him. But I let him drive me towards vengeance against you. I was so blind.
Let us work together. There is a world in which neither of us must suffer at each others' hands ever again.
It's what my father would have wanted—the right thing for Denmark. The county you and I both love.
But... what... do you intend to do?
We'll turn Claudius's plot back upon him.
At the moment he hands me the poisoned sword, I'll turn it upon his heart.
He won't expect it, and we'll soon be victorious.
Yes. I consent. I'll keep the ruse.
This-- Laertes-- you don't know how sweet these words are to hear from you.
Spare me the sentimentality. We still aren't friends. But I'll fight by your side all the same.
When next we meet, I hope it will be to take back our country. For good.
Aye. For good.
I don't want your death.
The destruction of your family line, and its undue influence upon my country.
Even if you prove to me that you can do otherwise. I know who you are. And who you have been, and will always be.
What I saw...
No. no, it's not possible.
It must be some trick Horatio pulled.
But why? How?
My God, what is happening?
Father? Are you there?
You've returned.
I promised myself I wouldn't, but something's changed.
My only desire is to remove my uncle from the throne of Denmark, as you bid me do.
And I had formed a plan to do that—in tandem with the playmaster Peter Quince.
Father, what do you know of that man? Do you have any reason to fear him?
Of course the spirit isn't here.
I truly have started to come apart, haven't I?
